scope.summary: Twenty-six independent offline Standard scans contributed to this aggregate. Findings cover production runtime, deployment ingress, telemetry, verification scripts, native tests, and the host benchmark self-test. The newest scan corroborated JA4 enforcement ordering and triggering-slot closure, identified a distinct JA4 baseline classification issue, and corroborated stale DNS incident family state. This additional independent scan corroborated the JA4 offender-closure and late Block All write paths, and identified a distinct loss of JA4 triggering-peer attribution across domains. The newest scan adds a conditional plain-DNS resolver origin risk and corroborates three established findings. The assigned scan corroborated the JA4 offender-closure, boot fixture, and benchmark B8 temp-file paths. The assigned worker independently corroborated the shutdown E2E no-admission false-pass path.

assumptions: No production deployment, operator config, firewall, resolver policy or collector configuration was supplied (README.md:92-101).

Reference appliance maps /config.toml with WORKDIR /, while local binary reads ./config.toml from its launch directory; there are no CLI/environment policy overrides (src/main.rs:14-17; docs/deployment.md:60-73,96-104).

Reference firewall permits upstream TCP 443 while proxy accepts configured ports 1..65535; non-443 entries need firewall change. This is a conditional availability mismatch (src/config/mod.rs:38-59,121-135; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2588-2607; docs/deployment.md:21-26).

Unpinned DoT has empty trust roots and fails closed; pinned DoT certificate validity outside the window is warning-only by documented design (src/dns/transport.rs:805-832; docs/trust-telemetry-design.md:87-89).
Proxy does not establish DNSSEC anchors or external resolver no-stale behavior; recursive_dnssec_policy is an operator declaration (src/config/mod.rs:631-643,667-690; README.md:64-73).
Reference host uses registry credential helper and DOCKER_CONFIG=/var/lib/docker/.docker; helper file permissions are outside inspected implementation (docs/deployment.md:96-104).
The reference QA harness stages /work/config.toml; the main binary still resolves config.toml against its process CWD (scripts/e2e_shutdown.py:775-783; src/main.rs:14-33).

Reference appliance adds writable ephemeral /tmp despite wording that it has no writable volumes; no production proxy /tmp write consumer was found (docs/deployment.md:103-120; docs/alumina-proxy.md:163).
The test-temp finding requires a shared writable temporary directory and host rules permitting symlink following; no actual test-host policy or runner privilege was supplied (src/log/tests.rs:21-35).

Document/config discrepancy: docs/deployment.md:116-120 says the host-network appliance binds 0.0.0.0:5353, but its Dockerfile copies an unspecified operator config and the supplied example binds 127.0.0.1:5353. Code binds the parsed value exactly (docs/deployment.md:60-66; docs/qa-package/config.example.toml:1-4; src/config/mod.rs:1184-1202; src/runtime/storage.rs:1658-1663).

Example resolver pins are explicitly placeholders; if copied unchanged, pinned DoT should fail identity checks. Actual pins are absent (docs/qa-package/config.example.toml:15-30; src/dns/transport.rs:810-823).
Documented systemd/image workflow is illustrative with placeholder registry and digest. Actual signing, account, image, firewall effect and config artifact are unverified (docs/deployment.md:45-114).
No operator config.toml, installed appliance, firewall, actual resolver, image, or stdout collector is supplied. The VPC pattern is conditional (README.md:92-105; docs/deployment.md:45-114).

Local example binds 127.0.0.1:5353; dedicated appliance describes 0.0.0.0:5353; binary binds configured value (docs/qa-package/config.example.toml:1-4; docs/deployment.md:116-120; src/runtime/storage.rs:1658-1663).

Example calls unpinned IP#fqdn CA-chain validating, but empty-root implementation fails closed; README and governing spec state this (docs/qa-package/config.example.toml:8-13; src/dns/transport.rs:784-832; README.md:51-55; docs/alumina-proxy.md:113).
Root-validating/no-stale policy is an operator declaration; proxy cannot establish resolver trust anchors, clock, or no-stale behavior (src/config/mod.rs:631-643,678-690; README.md:64-73).
Pinned DoT certificate validity-window mismatch warns while matching pin is accepted, expressly documented (src/dns/transport.rs:801-823; docs/alumina-proxy.md:1198-1202,1538-1542).
Config loader reads <cwd>/config.toml (src/main.rs:19-31; src/config/mod.rs:537-558); documented scratch container reads /config.toml via WORKDIR / and COPY (docs/deployment.md:45-73,96-103).

Bare-IP DNS uses <configured IP>:53 over plain TCP; unpinned FQDN uses <configured IP>:853 with empty roots; strict-pinned FQDN uses <configured IP>:853 with name and pin checks (src/dns/resolver.rs:184-230; src/dns/transport.rs:801-832,1674-1691,3199-3214).

Telemetry uses inherited stdout fd 1 and bounded nonblocking queue; actual sink/collector is deployment-owned. Appliance example uses Docker gcplogs (src/log/mod.rs:633-648; src/log/sink.rs:9-26; docs/deployment.md:96-104; docs/monitoring.md:3-9).
Documented privileged image workflow uses /var/lib/docker/.docker registry credentials and digest-pinned pull; installed unit and grants absent (docs/deployment.md:75-114).

attackerCapabilities: Compromised workload can issue arbitrary CONNECT and ClientHello bytes and attempt direct calls if deployment permits, but does not thereby own config, proxy, resolver or firewall (README.md:8-16; docs/deployment.md:3-36).

Untrusted DNS peer or compromised plain resolver can control replies; pinned DoT changes resolver-hop authentication, while DNSSEC root validation remains external (src/dns/resolver.rs:190-230; src/dns/transport.rs:805-832; README.md:51-55).

TCP peer reaching listener can consume bounded setup capacity and receive fixed refusal statuses; reachability is deployment controlled (src/runtime/tunnel.rs:43-57; src/runtime/reactor.rs:1876-1900).
Host operator can change image/config, collector, restart and firewall; this is preexisting authority (docs/deployment.md:45-73,96-113).

A local co-tenant may create entries in a shared writable temp directory, but cannot thereby control production proxy traffic or operator config; the test-file clobber additionally requires predictable placement, permitted symlink following, and a runner-writable target (src/log/tests.rs:21-35).

A compromised workload controls its CONNECT and ClientHello bytes and any direct network route left by deployment, but is not assumed to control config, host, resolver pin, or firewall (README.md:8-16; docs/deployment.md:3-7).

A listener-reachable party can send malformed or allowed-looking CONNECTs and consume bounded setup capacity; external reachability is unknown (src/runtime/reactor.rs:1876-1933; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:43-57).

A DNS/network adversary may influence plain TCP DNS, while pinned DoT and reply validation are separate controls; trusted config and declared recursive policy are not assumed compromised (src/dns/resolver.rs:184-230; src/dns/transport.rs:801-832; src/dns/wire.rs:1217-1277).
securityObjectives: Only exact configured FQDN:port may produce an upstream connection to an eligible current cache address before expiry (src/runtime/tunnel.rs:832-846,873-902; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2588-2634).

No tunnel bytes cross either direction until initial ClientHello passes TLS 1.3 profile, ECH and SNI checks; client verifies upstream certificate (src/runtime/gate.rs:7-23,114-127; src/inspection/client_hello.rs:874-886).

DNS publication preserves query identity/generation and per-entry assurance; strong modes require pins and declared external root-validating/no-stale resolver policy (src/config/mod.rs:631-643,667-690; src/dns/publication.rs:98-135; src/dns/cache.rs:925-947).
Tripwire block state and limits remain bounded and process-owned; deployment prevents direct egress and restart bypass (src/enforcement/state.rs:218-249; docs/deployment.md:3-43).
Logging cannot block the serving loop; operators collect stdout and detect loss (src/log/sink.rs:9-26,90-173; docs/monitoring.md:41-50).
Test sink files should be exclusively created in private or unpredictable temp locations so a lower-privilege local user cannot redirect truncation (src/runtime/owner/tests.rs:1116-1134).

Bind every dial to exact configured hostname:port and currently admissible DNS-derived eligible address with bounded attempts/deadlines (src/config/mod.rs:251-255; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:879-961; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2626-2644; src/eligibility.rs:38-83).
Prevent relay before validated ClientHello gate; preserve TLS 1.3, SNI and ECH policy (src/runtime/gate.rs:7-23; src/inspection/client_hello.rs:700-715,874-886).

Strong DNS assurance requires pinned resolvers and operator root-validating/no-stale declaration, not local DNSSEC validation (src/config/mod.rs:631-643,678-690; src/dns/cache.rs:516-528; README.md:64-89).

Maintain Linux privilege prerequisites, workload/appliance separation, bounded state, and rejection observability (src/boot/preflight.rs:88-112; docs/deployment.md:3-26; src/inventory.rs:10-49; docs/monitoring.md:3-9).

Configured JA4 Block Connection or Block Domain must stop the triggering tunnel before post-verdict upstream bytes; connect, setup, and idle deadlines must remain effective at their protected transitions.
Native test fixtures should claim private temporary files and directories exclusively and reject planted symlinks before writing config.toml or sink data.
Local unsafe-surface verification should account for all compiled production Rust through the admitted source paths, including symlinks.
When terminal records compete for bounded queue capacity, preserve the typed shutdown verdict according to an explicit priority policy.
Shutdown E2E case logs should be created inside a private, owned workspace with exclusive no-follow semantics.
Rearm the listener promptly when its bounded accept-error pause expires, even without unrelated readiness.
Listener accept backoff should enforce its 100 ms retry cadence and wake an otherwise quiet owner; live slot readiness must remain matchable after generation-field wrap on supported targets.
Associate each JA4 change fingerprint with its own triggering peer address in the per-domain monitor report.
threatModel.summary: Alumina is a Linux single-binary HTTP/1.1 CONNECT egress proxy. It reads CWD-relative config.toml, checks Linux privileges, initializes bounded DNS/cache/log/traffic storage, resolves configured allowlist names, binds a listener, and runs one owner loop for DNS refresh and client tunnels (src/main.rs:14-33,67-108; src/boot/mod.rs:83-98; src/runtime/storage.rs:349-373,1460-1496; src/runtime/owner.rs:1-9). Reference deployment uses a dedicated VM, host networking, an external VPC firewall and stdout collector; local QA may use loopback (docs/deployment.md:1-26,45-73,96-129; README.md:92-105). A later independent static scan identified a JA4 block-action bypass and deadline transition bypasses in the serving reactor; these are conditional on configured policy and precise timing, respectively. The latest scan also found a boot test fixture directory with a predictable path and nonexclusive child write, alongside previously identified truncating test log sinks. The newest review identified a distinct symlink traversal gap in the local unsafe-surface docs gate and a terminal logging priority issue that can displace shutdown_final under queue pressure. This scan confirmed a conditional listener retry delay after transient accept errors and a symlinked test-module bypass of the parentage gate. This follow-up also identified conditional 32-bit event-token generation truncation after repeated slot reuse; the published appliance targets x86_64. The latest independent review corroborated the JA4 block bypass and predictable test log path; both are accounted for in their established findings. The latest scan added a conditional subnet-wide reference ingress exposure and a missed early-activity telemetry path for combined upstream error/readiness events; actual deployment and event frequency remain unverified. The latest worker identified a separate false-pass path in the shutdown E2E no-admission witness: a reachable first post-signal connection can be forgotten if a second probe is refused; current proxy behavior was not reproduced. The newest worker also found a conditional shared pending-pool exhaustion path: incomplete CONNECT heads can occupy all 128 pending setups for up to ten seconds each and cause later clients to receive 503. The latest independent review found a distinct DNS incident reporting error: after full recovery, a later one-family incident can inherit the other family's earlier failure snapshot. The newest scan identifies a conditional DNS-derived destination redirection path when a bare-IP plain resolver and resolver_trusted assurance are used; actual operator configuration and on-path adversary position are unknown. The assigned worker corroborated the established JA4 offender-closure and shared-host boot and benchmark temp-file findings. The assigned reducer worker independently corroborated the shutdown E2E no-admission false-pass path.
trustBoundaries: Host/operator to proxy boot: config.toml is opened once, bounded to 16 KiB and validated; preflight rejects root UIDs, nonempty capabilities or missing no_new_privs. Host owns file permissions and process privileges (src/main.rs:14-33; src/config/mod.rs:537-586; src/boot/preflight.rs:88-139).

Workload/client to listener: bounded CONNECT parsing and exact normalized hostname:port allowlist matching gate the upstream dial. Configured tripwire actions form a separate enforcement path (src/inspection/connect.rs:229-251,370-401; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:768-782,873-902; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2470-2522).

Resolver to cache: configured numeric addresses use TCP 53 for bare IP or DoT 853 for FQDN; pinned DoT checks SAN and SPKI, unpinned DoT with empty roots fails closed. Parsing and publication enforce bounds, query identity, generation and assurance; plain DNS has no authenticated-origin proof (src/dns/resolver.rs:190-230; src/dns/transport.rs:805-832,1674-1691,2424-2438; src/dns/publication.rs:98-135).

Proxy to upstream: current admissible cache binding and approved port yield numeric TCP peer; dial rechecks binding and TLS ClientHello must match SNI/profile before relay. Client authenticates upstream TLS (src/runtime/tunnel.rs:832-846,873-902; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2588-2634,2797-2854; src/runtime/gate.rs:7-23).

Proxy to stdout collector: bounded nonblocking queue and loss accounting end at fd 1; collection and alerts are host responsibilities (src/log/mod.rs:1-15; src/log/sink.rs:9-26,90-173; docs/monitoring.md:41-50).

Workload versus deployment confinement: separate runtime/network identities and VPC firewall prevent direct egress and workload-controlled restarts; proxy owns CONNECT policy, not host firewall or lifecycle (docs/deployment.md:3-43; src/enforcement/state.rs:218-249).

Local co-tenant to test runner (conditional): test-only helpers derive PID/counter paths under std::env::temp_dir() and open with create+truncate; a preplaced symlink can redirect truncation if host symlink policy permits. Production serving does not call them (src/log/tests.rs:21-35; src/runtime/storage/startup_integration.rs:585-600; src/log/mod.rs:1041-1042; src/runtime/storage.rs:1672-1675).

Client to listener: any reachable TCP peer may send plaintext CONNECT without client authentication; bounded framing and exact normalized hostname:port membership govern authorization; Proxy-Authorization is ignored (src/runtime/reactor.rs:1876-1937; src/inspection/connect.rs:229-327; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:768-782; docs/alumina-proxy.md:78-83).

Reachable clients supply plaintext HTTP/1.1 CONNECT; an 8 KiB parser, exact allowlist pair check, DNS evidence, setup deadline, attempt limit, and per-dial peer admission govern upstream TCP opening (src/inspection/connect.rs:184-251; src/config/mod.rs:246-255; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:768-903; src/runtime/reactor.rs:2626-2644). No client source authentication is shown at accept; documented appliance ingress firewall owns reachability (src/runtime/reactor.rs:1876-1905; docs/deployment.md:22-26).

TLS ClientHello is a second boundary: TLS 1.3 offer, exactly one matching SNI, no ECH, and a two-barrier gate before relay (src/inspection/client_hello.rs:700-715,862-886; src/runtime/gate.rs:1-23,193-228). The client verifies upstream certificate (README.md:48-50).

Configured numeric resolvers supply DNS over TCP/53 or DoT/853. Pinned DoT verifies FQDN/SAN and SPKI; unpinned DoT uses empty roots and fails closed. Reply parser checks transaction/question identity and CNAME bailiwick. Plain TCP DNS lacks cryptographic origin authentication (src/config/mod.rs:667-717; src/dns/resolver.rs:184-230; src/dns/transport.rs:801-832,3199-3214; src/dns/wire.rs:1217-1277,1438-1485).
Linux process preflight requires non-root UIDs, no capabilities, and no_new_privs; deployment example supplies these host controls (src/boot/preflight.rs:88-129; docs/deployment.md:96-120).

CONNECT/parser/allowlist/TLS/ECH controls differ from per-domain early-data and JA4; class-specific gates govern all-scope latching (src/config/mod.rs:720-760,983-989; src/enforcement/state.rs:264-345).

Operator and host control config, firewall, image, registry credentials, and stdout collection. In-memory block state is not a host firewall; same-pod sidecar does not provide documented isolation (docs/deployment.md:3-43; README.md:56-62).

Within an admitted tunnel, JA4 baseline overflow and connect/setup/idle deadlines are enforcement boundaries. JA4 verdicts need to precede upstream forwarding; deadline checks need to guard the state transition and timer replacement (src/runtime/reactor.rs:2415-2425,2851-2905,2651-2660,2939,2981-3006).

Local co-tenant to native test runner (conditional): predictable PID/counter temp paths are used by log and startup test sinks and a boot fixture directory. Nonexclusive opens or reuse of a planted directory and config.toml child can overwrite runner-writable files if shared temp access and host permissions allow it (src/log/tests.rs:21-35; src/runtime/storage/startup_integration.rs:585-600; tests/support/temp_dir.rs:8-24).

Contributor-controlled repository source to local docs verification: a resolving production .rs symlink may be admitted while the preferred ripgrep unsafe scan omits its path; gate assurance depends on a reviewer or workflow using that local result (scripts/verify.sh:859-979).

Client-driven event pressure to terminal stdout reporting: a reserved monitor summary can displace a normal shutdown_final record on a near-full bounded queue; process exit status remains separately observable (src/runtime/owner.rs:30-40; src/log/queue.rs:206-227).

Local co-tenant to host benchmark verifier (conditional): the documented host self-test defaults to /tmp and writes fixed output and TLS artifact paths; planted symlinks can redirect runner writes if shared temp access and host symlink policy permit (docs/benchmarks/e2micro-suite.md:184-190; scripts/bench_workload.py:2079-2097,2710-2715,3402-3403).

Local co-tenant to shutdown E2E runner (conditional): fixed /tmp/shutdown-{name}.log opens with wb may follow a planted symlink to a runner-writable target when the cases execute in a shared temporary namespace (scripts/e2e_shutdown.py:809-810,1252).
Client and OS accept pressure to listener availability: after transient accept error the reactor's retry deadline must wake polling and rearm queued clients (src/runtime/reactor.rs:1536,1900,3272).

Contributor-controlled module declarations and symlinked test leaves to the local docs gate: every admitted test-named path must have actual cfg(test) parentage before unsafe exemption (scripts/verify.sh:872,896,934).

Listener clients to slot readiness on a 32-bit build: per-slot u64 generations are packed into usize event tokens, whose 21-bit generation field can wrap before the stored counter (src/runtime/reactor.rs:1920-1933,3399-3406).

Local shutdown E2E harness to no-admission verdict: a post-SIGTERM reachable connect must remain a failing observation across subsequent samples; probe_refused_sampled currently substitutes a second probe (scripts/e2e_shutdown.py:147-190,226-239,1047,1204).

Reachable listener peers share one pending setup pool without per-peer quotas. A peer can hold slots with incomplete CONNECT heads until the ten-second setup deadline; availability impact requires another client sharing the listener (src/inspection/connect.rs:241-251; src/runtime/tunnel.rs:439-452).

Resolver failure and recovery outcomes to operator incident telemetry: a newly opened window should report only the current A/AAAA family snapshots; stale state from a closed window can misattribute a later incident (src/runtime/storage.rs:784-828; src/dns/incident_report.rs:98-109,321-342,467-481).
